name: Temporomandibular Disorder (TMD)
summary: Education, jaw exercise, habit modification and selected manual therapy can improve pain and function in musculoskeletal TMD.

redFlags: Neurological symptoms or unexplained weight loss
firstSteps: Measure comfortable mouth opening and pain with chewing/yawning.
Assess deviation, joint sounds, masticatory tenderness and cervical function.
selfCare: Temporarily modify very hard/chewy foods if needed

stages.label: Start: assess and set up
stages.goal: Treat musculoskeletal TMD with jaw-control exercise, habit modification and selected manual therapy.
do: Measure comfortable mouth opening and pain with chewing/yawning.
Assess deviation, joint sounds, masticatory tenderness and cervical function.
Assess: Jaw opening pattern and range
moveOn: Baseline recorded: Maximum comfortable mouth opening
Baseline recorded: Jaw Functional Limitation Scale

stages.label: Treat: build capacity
stages.goal: Screen dental/maxillofacial causes and true locking.
when: Baseline recorded: Maximum comfortable mouth opening
dose: Controlled opening with tongue resting gently on palate: 6–10 reps, 2–4 times/day.
Jaw isometrics: gentle 5-second holds × 5 reps in selected directions.
Cervical/scapular exercise: 2–3 sets × 8–15 reps if relevant.
moveOn: Increase chewing tolerance and range gradually
Add resistance when pain is stable

stages.label: Progress and self-manage
stages.goal: Cervical contribution can matter in some patients.
when: Increase chewing tolerance and range gradually
Add resistance when pain is stable
do: Temporarily modify very hard/chewy foods if needed
dose: Progress jaw resistance only when baseline pain is stable.
Reduce manual therapy as self-management improves.

manual: Gentle TMJ distraction or glide when mobility restriction is present.
Masseter/temporalis soft-tissue work using tolerable pressure.
Cervical mobilization only if it changes the comparable jaw/neck symptom.
modalities: TENS may be trialed in selected pain-dominant presentations
Heat 10–15 minutes can help muscle-dominant pain; TENS is optional.
progression: Increase chewing tolerance and range gradually
Add resistance when pain is stable
Progress jaw resistance only when baseline pain is stable.
Reduce manual therapy as self-management improves.
mistakes: Treating joint sounds that are painless and not functionally limiting.
education: Temporarily modify very hard/chewy foods during flares.
Teach relaxed jaw posture and controlled movement.
escalation: Dental/maxillofacial review for locking, trauma, structural disorder or persistent severe symptoms
